paper.title: Dynamic Assortment Optimization with Changing Contextual Information

settings.name_in_paper: Dynamic assortment optimization under changing contextual MNL model
unmapped: Multinomial logit (MNL) choice feedback: the customer purchases one item from the offered assortment (or nothing) with probability exp(v_tj^T theta_0)/(1+sum_k exp(v_tk^T theta_0)); only the purchased item is observed
Expected revenue of an assortment is a nonlinear (MNL) function of item utilities; revenues r_tj in [0,1] revealed each round
Features v_tj i.i.d. from a nondegenerate distribution (lambda_min(E vv^T) >= lambda_0) during the pure-exploration phase, adversarial afterwards
Assumption (A2): ratio of choice probabilities bounded by rho; ||v_tj|| <= nu; learner's tuning uses rho, nu, lambda_0
Paper's N (number of items) is mapped to K; paper's cardinality constraint K is mapped to m
settings.definition_quote: At each time $t$, a set of time-sensitive ``feature vectors'' $v_{t1}, v_{t2}, \cdots, v_{tN}\in\mathbb R^d$ and revenues $r_{t1},\cdots,r_{tN}\in[0,1]$ are observed... A retailer ... picks an assortment $S_t\subseteq[N]$ under the cardinality constraint $|S_t|\leq K$ ... then observes a purchasing action $i_t\in S_t\cup\{0\}$ and collects the associated revenue

settings.name_in_paper: Dynamic assortment optimization under changing contextual MNL model (lower bound)
unmapped: Multinomial logit (MNL) choice feedback: only the purchased item (or no purchase) is observed
Expected revenue is a nonlinear MNL function of item utilities
Paper's N (number of items) is mapped to K; paper's cardinality constraint K is mapped to m
settings.definition_quote: Our lower bound is information theoretical, and therefore applies to \emph{any} policy for dynamic assortment optimization with changing contextual features.

algorithms.name: MLE-UCB with an (alpha, epsilon, delta)-approximation oracle for the combinatorial step

bound.expression_latex: C_1\left[ d\sqrt{T}\cdot \log(\lambda_0^{-1}\rho\nu TK)+ {d^2\lambda_0^{-2}\rho^4\nu^2 K^2\log T}\right] + C_2

symbols.rho: bound on ratio of MNL choice probabilities (Assumption A2)
symbols.lambda_0: lower bound on lambda_min(E v v^T) of the exploration-phase feature distribution

conditions: (A1): ||v_tj||_2 <= nu for all t,j; for t <= T_0 features i.i.d. from a distribution with lambda_min(E vv^T) >= lambda_0
tuning: T_0 ~ max{nu^2 d log T/lambda_0^2, rho^2 (d+log T)/(tau^2 lambda_0)}
omega ~ sqrt(d log(rho nu T m))

results.notes: Regret defined via expected revenues R_t(S), i.e. pseudo-regret against the per-round optimal assortment. Universal constants recorded via O notation. Exact step-7 optimization enumerates all subsets (not polynomial); paper's K renamed m. No dependence on number of items N.

conditions: features invariant over time; revenues r_ti = 1

source.label: thm:lower
source.quote: Suppose $d$ is divisible by 4. There exists a universal constant $C_0>0$ such that for any sufficiently large $T$ and policy $\pi$, there is a worst-case problem instance with $N\asymp K\cdot 2^d$ items and uniformly bounded feature and coefficient vector (i.e., $\|v_{ti}\|_2\leq 1$ and $\|\theta_0\|_2\leq 1$ ...) such that the regret of $\pi$ is lower bounded by $C_2\cdot d\sqrt{T}/K$.

results.notes: Paper's K renamed m. Features are fixed across time in the construction.

symbols.alpha_approx: multiplicative approximation factor of the combinatorial oracle
symbols.eps_approx: additive approximation error of the oracle
symbols.delta_approx: failure probability of the oracle per round

tuning: same T_0, tau, omega as Theorem 1

source.label: lem:approx
source.quote: Suppose an $(\alpha,\varepsilon,\delta)$-approximation algorithm is used instead of exact optimization in the MLE-UCB policy at each time period $t$. Then its regret can be upper bounded by $\alpha\cdot \mathrm{Regret}^* + \varepsilon T + \delta T^2 + O(1)$

results.notes: Reduction lemma; Appendix uses it with a randomized DP approximation (alpha = sqrt(d), eps = T^{-1/2}, delta = T^{-2}) running in polynomial time per round, giving O(sqrt(d))·Regret*. Compute 'polynomial' refers to that instantiation.
